full_judgment:
8. The affidavit-in-opposition submitted on behalf of the EC (Res.2) reveals that pursuant to the direction made by this Court an enquiry was held at the instance of the EC by the District Election Officer, Noakhali. In the enquiry conducted by the District Election Officer irregularities and corrupt practices materially affecting purity of election were found in respect of center Nos. 3 and 7 and recommendations for re-poll in those two centres were made. As for center Nos. 2, 5 and 6, the inquiry officer found no mentionable irregularity as is complained of by the petitioner. The affidavit further suggests that regardless of the unprecedented incidents that happened resulting in postponement of election as many as in four centres and recommendation for re-poll in two other centres by the enquiry officer the EC remained unconcerned about the report and chose not to make any comment on it disclosing its mind. Rather it seems to be obsessed by the impression that the Appellate Division has already settled the law putting a total bar on the High Court Division in entertaining writ petition challenging any of the steps in the electoral-process and sat tight on the single defense on maintainability of writ petition understandably keeping in view the case of AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Haq, 61 DLR (AD) 68. 

 32. VI) CP Nos. 53 & 59 of 1992: this case indicates a standard for interference by the EC. Both the appeals, one filed by the EC and another by the candidate who was declared elected,, arose out of the same writ petition. This case also relates to the election to the office of chairman, union parishad. Election was held in three centres on 25 January, 1992. Presiding Officer after counting the votes forwarded the result to the Returning Officer. Returning Officer in his turn consolidated the result and declared the candidate securing highest votes elected. But the EC cancelled the election of one centre and directed re-poll on the ground that the result was blatantly manipulated by the presiding Officer. This order was challenged in a writ petition which was allowed and the Commission's order was set aside. In this case EC acted on the basis of admitted records and found that the presiding office, after counting the ballot-papers in presence of the parties, gave two contradictory reports on the result of counting. The anomaly was not explained satisfactorily. At the first counting the presiding Officer found 950 ballot papers missing and issued certificate to that effect as demanded by some of the candidates present on the spot. After few hours presiding Officer counted the ballot papers again and found only two ballot-papers missing. Case of the contesting candidate affected by the result is that the 950 ballot-papers that were initially shown missing contained his votes and it is the presiding Officer who did the mischief.
